Research dossier: FN — Fabrinet

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.68 · Opportunity score: 71

Next earnings: 2026-08-24

Business

Thailand-based precision contract manufacturer of optical and electro-mechanical packages — the

company that physically assembles and tests high-speed optical transceivers (800G now, 1.6T

ramping) and related photonics for other people's brands. Customers are the optical/networking

primes and, increasingly, the chip vendor itself: NVIDIA (~30% of revenue, sell-side sees up to

~50% annualized), plus Cisco, Coherent, Lumentum, Ciena, and a named direct hyperscaler

relationship (AWS, plus two newer direct datacom programs ramping through FY27). FN reportedly

holds a majority-to-~100% share on the 1.6T transceivers feeding NVIDIA's Blackwell platform

(one March 2026 Barclays note flagged "great uncertainty" on Blackwell 1.6T timing, but that call

is now four months stale and has been superseded by two subsequent Barclays PT raises — $537

in Jan → $702 in May — i.e. Barclays itself walked the caution back). Revenue durably continues

because FN owns scarce precision-manufacturing capacity and yield/quality entrenchment primes

don't want to rebuild — they design the optics, FN builds them. It is a **substrate /

picks-and-shovels** play in the orchestration-vs-substrate frame: real earnings, but thin

(~10% net) contract-manufacturing margins and limited IP/pricing power. Unchanged since the last

dive.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The business is unchanged; the price has kept falling, and it did so exactly on the schedule the

6/27 and 7/4 dossiers pre-committed to. Since the 7/4 dive (BUY at $499.61, add-toward-lower-end),

FN has taken a third leg down: last close $471.13-$471.16 (screen 7/11), off 36.9%

from the 52-week high (was 33.0% on 7/4), -9.8% vs the 200DMA (was -3.7% — the break below

trend has deepened, not reversed), ret_60d -30.9%. The 7/4 dossier explicitly wrote: *"A

third cohort-wide leg to ~$470 with the group still moving together → add again, same thesis,

better price."* That is precisely what happened, and the cohort-confirmation test still passes:

AAOI/COHR/LITE fell again together (AAOI -17% to $114.93, COHR -10% to $331.57, LITE -10% to

$720.91 around 7/1-7/2), and a broader semiconductor selloff hit July 6-7 after Samsung's Q2

print — a 19x profit beat that still triggered an 8% Samsung drop and a >$1.3T sector-wide

semi wipeout (SOX -7-10% since 6/22) because DRAM pricing came in softer than the market's

extrapolated-forever assumption. That catalyst is about memory pricing, one step further

removed from FN's actual product (optics assembly, not DRAM) than the prior two legs, which were

at least inside the optics cohort itself. No FN-specific news surfaced in this window: no new

downgrade, no guidance change, no confirmed customer-share loss. Per macro-cohort-confirmation,

a third macro/cohort-wide leg with zero idiosyncratic news is still liquidity, not information.

**BUY, add — this is the third pre-committed add point, not a fresh idea, and the discount is now

deeper than either prior entry.**

Valuation + position vs. range

  • Price ~$471 ($471.13 stockanalysis 7/10 close, $471.16 screen); market cap $16.88B;

52-wk range $272.49–$748.89 (off-high 36.9%, +72.2% above the low). ret_20d -18.8%,

ret_60d -30.9%, -24.2% vs 50DMA, -9.8% vs 200DMA — now solidly, not marginally,

below the 200-day trend line.

  • Trailing P/E 40.47, forward P/E 28.75 (down from 30.49 three weeks ago, down from 32.0

five weeks ago — a straight-line multiple compression across three legs with the same TTM

fundamentals). Revenue TTM $4.24B (+29.8%); net income TTM $420.97M (+29.0%); EPS TTM

$11.64; ~35.83M shares. Implied NTM EPS ~$16.4 (471.13 / 28.75), essentially

unchanged from the last two dives — the multiple moved, not the earnings estimate.

  • My fair-value read, unchanged methodology: 30–35× forward on a ~30%-grower with

single-customer concentration and a CPO hedge (Raytek) → $492–$574. At ~$471 the market now

pays 28.75× NTM — below the floor of that band for the first time across three dives (was

bottom-of-band at 30.5× on 7/4, mid-band at 32.0× on 6/27). Sell-side average 12-mo PT sits at

Post-deal / repriced check

Not a Wait-for-deal thesis name, but the repriced discipline applies and has now moved a

third increment in the buyer's favor: the de-rate that "fully opened" at $525 on 6/27 and reached

the "bottom of the band" at $500 on 7/4 has now **broken through the bottom of the fair band

entirely** at $471, still with no fundamentally new negative FN-specific information. Three

consecutive cohort/macro legs down is the point where the falsification note from 7/4 said the

"structural repricing vs. dip" question needs to be taken seriously rather than dismissed — this

dive treats it seriously by (a) confirming the newest leg's catalyst (Samsung DRAM miss) is

memory-specific and one degree further from FN's actual optics-assembly business than the prior

legs, and (b) confirming credit markets are still not reacting (macro.md: BBB ~100bp, HY

~267-285bp, unmoved through the entire window including the Iran/oil episode). Two independent

non-FN, non-optics catalysts (Meta Compute report, Samsung DRAM miss) producing three legs of the

same cohort de-rate is unusual, but it is still a multiple story, not an FN earnings story —

nothing in this window contradicts FN's own Q3 FY26 print (+39% YoY, telecom record $628.3M) or

the 1.6T Blackwell ramp.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: Sole-scale assembler of the exact 1.6T optics the AI buildout needs, +39% and

accelerating, now three cohort/macro legs into a de-rate that has pushed the multiple through

the bottom of a reasonable 30-35× band to 28.75× with zero FN-specific bad news across any of

the three legs and Street targets unchanged ~59% above spot — this is the best absolute price

either of the two prior dives got.

  • Bear: Three consecutive legs down in five weeks, each blamed on "someone else's" news

(cohort valuation, Meta Compute, Samsung DRAM), is exactly the pattern a genuine regime change

looks like in real time before anyone admits it — a ~10%-margin contract manufacturer with

30-50% revenue concentration on one customer does not deserve the benefit of the doubt

indefinitely, and "it's not about us" narrated three times in a row is what a broken chart

sounds like from the inside.

  • First-principles: A capacity-and-yield business with no IP moat and one dominant customer

is worth ~30-35× only while the pluggable cycle and that customer's volume hold; at 28.75× fwd

with +30% growth, three cohort/macro-confirmed legs, and still no fundamental deterioration in

FN's own numbers, the price now pays more margin of safety than fair for the concentration

risk — but the falsification bar (a fourth leg, or any FN-specific negative) is closer than it

was three weeks ago simply because less room remains before "structural reset" has to be taken

literally rather than provisionally.

Falsification

  • 30-day: A fourth cohort/macro-wide leg to ~$450 with the group still moving together →

add again, same thesis, better price, but flag explicitly that four legs is the point to

reweight toward "structural" over "dip." A bounce back above ~$525-540 with no new catalyst →

stop adding, edge re-consumed. Any FN-specific bad news (a real NVIDIA-share loss, a margin

  • 90-day: A concrete CPO adoption signal that bypasses FN (a hyperscaler/NVIDIA CPO switch

NVDABUYfetched62›

Research dossier: NVDA — NVIDIA Corp

Researched: 2026-06-27 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.62 · Opportunity score: 62

Next earnings: 2026-08-26

Business

NVIDIA sells the accelerated-compute substrate for AI: data-center GPUs (Blackwell B200/B300,

Rubin ramping), the networking that lashes them into clusters (InfiniBand, Spectrum-X, NVLink),

and the CUDA software moat that keeps the ecosystem sticky. Customers are the hyperscalers

(~50% of Data Center revenue), plus a widening tail of AI clouds, sovereigns, enterprise and

industrial. Per Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability and GPU Economics, durability is the only

question that matters for the valuation, and it rests on two legs: (a) hyperscaler capex

continuing to ramp, and (b) GPU economics — rental price and useful life — staying firm. Both

are still standing, but both took a knock this month (see below).

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Qualified yes, but lower-conviction than two weeks ago. The fundamental floor is intact and the

valuation is the most attractive it's been: Q1 FY27 (2026-05-20) was a real acceleration —

revenue $81.6B (+85% YoY), Data Center a record $75.2B (+92%), and Q2 guided to $91B

(~+11% sequential), paired with an $80B buyback and a 25× dividend raise. China H20 is already

zeroed from the run-rate (pure upside optionality). None of that has broken.

What changed since the 2026-06-13 dossier, and why I'm marking down:

  • The catalyst went stale. The May-20 print is now 5+ weeks old. The macro discipline

(extended-with-vs-without-catalyst) wants a real dip OR a fresh catalyst. We now have

the dip but no fresh catalyst — the new news flow is net-negative (below), and the next

thesis event is the Aug-26 print, two months out. A stale-catalyst dip is the weaker of the

two BUY conditions.

  • NVDA is the laggard, not the leader. It's the worst-performing major semi YTD (~+3.65%)

while the SOX is ~+70%, Micron ~+284%, AMD ~+138%. Capital rotated into memory/HBM and ASIC

beneficiaries. That underperformance is itself the opportunity-cost case (cheapest, highest

quality, de-rated) — but it also tells you the market is actively re-pricing NVDA's share of

the AI dollar downward, which is a signal, not just noise.

  • The ASIC share-shift is now visible in the guide. Custom silicon is ~28% of 2026

hyperscaler capex (~$185B, up from <$30B in 2022); TrendForce sees custom-chip sales +45% in

2026 vs GPU shipments +16%. NVDA's own FY27 outlook bakes in ~18% growth (vs 112% FY26). The

Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability essay's counter still holds — GPUs win on useful-life/financing

vs single-purpose ASICs, and custom growing off a tiny base doesn't shrink NVDA's pie — but the

durability question now has a real, market-visible data point against it, which the prior

dossier underweighted.

  • GPU cloud-rental is softening (kill-switch #2 yellow flag, NOT tripped — see Macro fit).

So: a genuine value setup in the single best AI franchise, on a real ~18% pullback to its

200-DMA — but bought into a hawkish-Fed/extended-market tape with a stale catalyst and a growing

(if overstated) ASIC overhang. That's a BUY you stage and trigger-gate, not one you chase at

market. Dip-buyer base rate supports the setup but demands humility: **33 instances, 67.7% win

at +21/42/63d, avg +12.4% at +63d, but worst-case -45.2% and avg max drawdown -11.8%.**

Valuation + position vs. range

Price $192.53 (close 2026-06-26); market cap $4.66T; **trailing P/E 29.5, forward P/E

19.4 (fetched, stockanalysis.com); TTM revenue $253.5B (+70.7%), net income $159.6B

(+108%), 24.22B shares. Implied forward EPS ≈ $9.94. Screen: 18.8% off the 52-wk high**

(ATH $235.47 on 2026-05-14), +26.7% above the low, sitting right on its 200-DMA

(+0.7%) and -8.6% below the 50-DMA — mid-range, decidedly not extended.

The standout fact persists and has gotten stronger: the single largest AI beneficiary trades

at a forward multiple (~19.4×) BELOW the S&P 500 itself (~20–22×) — cheaper than the 20.7×

in the 6/13 read — while growing revenue 70%+ and earnings 100%+. My fair-value read: a clean,

cash-generative, buyback-supported grower of this quality earns more than a market multiple even

after haircutting for the ASIC share-shift. At a conservative 22× forward EPS that's ~$219; the

market is paying ~19.4×, pricing in a deceleration sharper than the Q2 guide shows. **Much is

priced in on growth; the multiple is now pricing in active share-loss — that gap is the edge,

but it's a thinner edge than before because the share-loss concern is real, not imagined.**

Post-deal / repriced check

Wait-for-deal thesis doesn't apply cleanly — NVDA is the substrate collecting the capex,

not a small provider waiting on one lab's offtake to reprice it; there's no single deal whose

announcement consumed the entry edge. On the ai-capex-payback-window J-curve, NVDA is on the

right side: it books the cash now (positive FCF, fortress balance sheet); the FCF compression

is the customers' problem. The relevant repricing here is the multiple — and it has moved the

right way for a buyer (compressed to a sub-market 19.4× forward), which is what makes this an

entry candidate rather than a chase. The thesis break would be kill-switch #1 (customers cutting

capex) — not visible; capex still +77% YoY and being raised.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: The best AI franchise on earth, a 100%-earnings-grower with a CUDA moat and an $80B

buyback, trading at a below-market forward multiple after an 18% pullback to its 200-DMA —

the cohort laggard, not the leader.

  • Bear: The AI dollar is visibly migrating to custom silicon (~28% of capex, +45% growth),

cloud-rental is rolling over, insiders dumped $410M in 3 months, and the FY27 guide already

concedes 18% growth — the durability question is being answered the wrong way in real time.

  • First-principles: At 19× forward earnings of a business compounding 70%+ with the world

still short watts and wafers through 2027, you're underpaying for the durability — unless

ASICs structurally cap NVDA's share, in which case 19× is a value trap on a decelerating peak.

Entry levels the agent derives

Re-derived this run from $192.53 and forward EPS ≈ $9.94 (every level recomputed; no anchor

carried from the 6/13 run):

  • Buy-below: $188 (≈19× forward — at/just under the 200-DMA; buy the quality laggard at a

sub-market multiple, but demand a hair of margin given no fresh catalyst + ASIC overhang).

  • Fair: $219 (~22× forward).
  • Stretch: $245 (~24.6× forward, near the ATH — do NOT pay up here without a fresh

thesis-confirming catalyst, i.e. the Aug-26 print).

Execution shape: stage it, trigger-gated. A partial near $185–190 (at/under the 200-DMA),

holding dry powder to add into a cohort-de-rate flush toward $170–178 (~17× forward, ~26% off

high) — only if it's macro/cohort-wide (macro-cohort-confirmation), not an NVDA-specific

crack like a kill-switch trip. The -45% worst-case in the base rate is the reason not to commit

the full clip at market with the next catalyst two months out.

Macro fit

Kill-switches (ai-infra-thesis-kill-switches): #1 capex clear (+77% YoY, being raised);

#3 credit clear (HY OAS ~276bp, 2.2× headroom). #2 GPU pricing is the watch item this run —

one B200 cloud-rental index fell ~$6.11→$4.22/hr (~31%) over a month, but broad on-demand still

Business

Largest US electricity producer post-Calpine. ~32GW of generation, anchored by the country's

fleet acquired Jan 2026 ($16.4B, 50M shares issued). Who pays them: wholesale power markets

(PJM capacity + energy), state ZEC programs, retail load, and — increasingly — direct hyperscaler

PPAs. The durable revenue is irreplaceable 24/7 baseload: AI data centers need firm carbon-free

power that the grid physically cannot add fast enough (AI Energy Thesis, permitting-as-binding-constraint).

Research dossier: APP — AppLovin Corporation

Researched: 2026-06-26 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 56

Business

AppLovin runs a two-sided mobile advertising marketplace. Its AXON AI engine ingests real-time

bid signals from app publishers and matches them to advertiser demand at very low latency,

producing far higher install-to-ad-spend ROI than competing networks. Revenue is now almost

entirely the Software Platform (AXON + MAX mediation) after the legacy Apps/games portfolio was

sold down. Who pays: mobile app marketers — historically gaming studios, now expanding into

e-commerce/consumer brands. The flywheel is data-compounding: every impression feeds AXON,

improving match quality, which raises advertiser ROI, which attracts more spend, which feeds

more data. For 14 years AXON was closed/invite-only; that gate comes off in June 2026.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**This run flips the prior HOLD to a BUY, because the two things the June-5 dossier was waiting

for both happened: the price came to fair value, and the catalyst went live.**

What changed since the last dive (HOLD at ~$571):

  • Price: ~$477 (June 26, +7% on the day), down ~36% off the 52w high (~$745) and -20.6%

over 20 days — squarely in the dip-buyer zone (-4% vs 50DMA, -11.9% vs 200DMA). Market cap

fell ~$190B → ~$160B.

insider selling (CEO Adam Foroughi ~$25.8M across June 10/12; director Vivas June 16 — read

as profit-taking after a huge run, still holding millions, not a wholesale exit), and broad

SaaS-sector weakness. The business prints kept beating.

self-serve has run since Oct 1 2025; June removes the gate so any advertiser worldwide can

sign up. This is the genuine business-model inflection — gaming → e-commerce, a multiples-larger

TAM at ~zero incremental infra cost. Per extended-with-vs-without-catalyst, a fact about

the business changed; this is a fresh catalyst, not FOMO.

beat $3.42. TTM revenue $6.16B (+66%); TTM net income $3.96B.

Research dossier: AVGO — Broadcom Inc.

Researched: 2026-06-30 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.58 · Opportunity score: 55

Next earnings: 2026-09-03

Business

Broadcom is two businesses fused: (1) Semiconductors (~$15B/qtr, the growth engine) — it

co-designs custom AI accelerators (XPUs) with individual hyperscalers and sells the **AI

networking silicon** (Tomahawk/Jericho switches, optics) that stitches thousands of those chips

into a cluster. Six core custom-silicon customers, publicly including Google, Meta, OpenAI and

Anthropic. (2) Infrastructure software (~$7B/qtr, the cash ballast) — VMware plus the legacy

CA/Symantec stack, sold as sticky enterprise subscriptions. The XPU + switch-fabric position is a

genuine orchestration-vs-substrate substrate play at the silicon layer: whoever builds the

cluster pays Broadcom regardless of which lab wins the model race. That's why the revenue durably

continues — picks-and-shovels — and unlike the hyperscalers it is FCF-positive right now, not

underwater in the ai-capex-payback-window J-curve.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Yes, on a staged basis — the entry gate the Jun-23 run said was closed has re-opened. That run

landed HOLD/47 explicitly because the Jun-3 earnings catalyst had aged out and the price (~$380)

was only ~fair. Its own 60-day falsification named the exact event that would flip it back to BUY:

"a fresh catalyst — a new XPU customer, an FY26 AI raise, or a named multi-year offtake."

That event landed June 24: Broadcom and OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño, OpenAI's first custom

LLM-inference ASIC, as the first piece of a plan to deploy **~10 GW of OpenAI-designed accelerators

between 2H-2026 and end-2029** — taped out in ~9 months (claimed fastest high-performance ASIC

cycle ever). This is a named, multi-year offtake with a deployment schedule, not a reaffirm. It

converts OpenAI from "one of six logos on a slide" into a productized, scheduled revenue stream and

hard-confirms the durability of the XPU pipeline through the back half of the decade.

The reason this is a buy and not a chase (extended-with-vs-without-catalyst): the catalyst is

6 days old (well inside the catalyst window) and the stock did not re-rate on it — it popped

~2% intraday and sits at $377.75, still ~24% off its $495 high and in the dip-buyer zone

(−8.1% vs 50DMA). So I am buying a de-rated quality name into a fresh positive catalyst, which

is the opposite of paying up for one already priced. The honest counterweight: Jalapeño's revenue is

"modest in FY26, meaningful in FY27" — back-half-loaded — and OpenAI was already a known XPU

customer, so this concretizes rather than expands the logo count. It earns the upgrade, but a

measured one.

FSLRBUYfetched55›

Research dossier: FSLR — First Solar

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 55

Next earnings: 2026-07-23

Business

First Solar is the largest US-domiciled solar module maker, building thin-film cadmium-telluride (CdTe) panels rather than the polysilicon modules that dominate globally — a technology that structurally sidesteps the silicon trade war and the pending Section 232 polysilicon case. Revenue is ~96% US, from domestic fabs in Ohio, Alabama, and Louisiana plus older Malaysia/Vietnam capacity now running at deliberately low utilization (~20%) to avoid reciprocal tariffs. Customers are utility-scale developers and corporate clean-energy buyers on multi-year, fixed-price, take-or-pay contracts. The P&L rides two US policy levers: (1) Section 45X manufacturing credits (~$0.17/W thin-film; FY26 EBITDA guide $2.6–2.8B is still credit-heavy), sold for cash (>$2.0B transferred to date); (2) tariffs (Section 201 expired Feb 2026; 301/AD-CVD plus a pending Section 232 polysilicon case) that wall off Chinese/SE-Asian supply. Demand durability is real (contracted backlog + AI-driven electricity growth); the risk is concentrated in policy and litigation overhang, not end-demand.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

This is the third dossier on this name in three weeks (6/25 HOLD → 7/3 BUY → today), so the job tonight is mostly stress-testing the 7/3 BUY call rather than re-deriving from scratch. The 7/3 dive flipped to BUY on a real dip (price through both DMAs, −29.9% off high) plus a still-unfired Section 232 catalyst, sized small against a lawsuit + insider-selling overhang. Eight trading days later:

1. Price has round-tripped sideways, not resolved either way. $224.57 (7/2) → $227.71–227.83 (7/10 close, per screen and stockanalysis). Off-52w-high has actually widened slightly to 28.9% (52w high itself likely ticked, or rounding), still below both the 50dma (vs_50dma −8.3%) and closer to the 200dma (vs_200dma −3.3%, materially tighter than the 7/3 read's −8.3%/−4.4% split — the 200dma has been drifting down toward spot). Net: still squarely in the dip_buyer entry shape, not yet reverted.

2. The Section 232 catalyst did NOT resolve on the 7/4 date the 7/3 dossier flagged — it's now firmly dated to early August. Roth Capital Partners (via pv-magazine-usa, 6/22, and corroborated in this week's Wells Fargo note) has the White House proclamation slipping from late-June/early-July expectations to early August 2026. This is a delay, not a cancellation, and sell-side has gotten more bullish on the outcome in the interim, not less (see below) — but it means the binary the prior dossier expected "any day" is now confirmed to land roughly 3-4 weeks out, likely straddling the 7/23 Q2 print.

3. Sell-side has moved decisively bullish since 7/3, which the 7/3 dossier didn't have. Wells Fargo raised FSLR to $320 PT from $255 (7/6, "asymmetric upside" framing on the Section 232 outcome) and Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy from Neutral with a $272 PT (7/7). Consensus PT has ticked up to $251.26 (from $247.30) even as spot barely moved — two fresh, dated, catalyst-specific upgrades from desks explicitly modeling the CdTe-favorable Section 232 scenario is a real (if lagging, sell-side-driven) confirmation of the 7/3 thesis, not new information the market has already priced — spot is flat since the upgrades.

4. The insider-selling tell has NOT worsened, and July's Form 4 activity is neutral, not confirmatory-bearish. The 7/7 resolved-thread finding (already in this pipeline's ledger) established the 135-sells/0-buys pattern was a routine 10b5-1 plan adopted 8 months before either catalyst went live — not a front-run signal. This week's Form 4 filings (director grants to Ahearn, Post, Renduchintala, Morgan, ~223-313 shares each) are ordinary quarterly non-employee-director equity compensation, not open-market sales. No fresh insider buying, but no fresh insider dumping either — the overhang is unchanged, not deepening.

5. **New, smaller item worth naming: a 45X extension draft (distinct from the current, already-legislated 45X credit) has reportedly slipped past the midterms** per the same Roth Capital note. This is about extending 45X's structure/duration further into the future, not touching the credit that's driving the FY26 $2.6-2.8B EBITDA guide today — a watch item for 2027+ credit durability, not a change to the near-term thesis.

6. The 2023 precedent is worth citing for the first time: First Solar previously won full dismissal-with-prejudice of an earlier securities class action (Series 6 cost-per-watt claims, dismissed June 2023). Different facts, not a guarantee of the same outcome here, but it's evidence this management/board has a track record of the earlier case not sticking — a data point tempering, not resolving, the current litigation risk.

Net: the core 7/3 case is intact and modestly reinforced — sell-side has moved bullish on the pending catalyst, insider selling hasn't escalated, and the price hasn't run away (still sitting right at the derived buy-below). The catalyst is later than hoped (early August vs. "any day") and now sits close to earnings (7/23), which stacks two binaries in a three-week window rather than resolving one cleanly first. Conviction stays at BUY but unchanged/slightly capped, not raised, given the stacked-catalyst timing risk and zero net new fundamental information since 7/3.

Falsification

5-10 day: No major near-term trigger expected before earnings; watch for any acceleration of the Section 232 timeline (a surprise early announcement would be the single biggest near-term mover either direction).

20-day (7/23 earnings): Q2 print — Malaysia/Vietnam underutilization charges (guided to stay elevated), 45X credit sales pace, bookings/backlog commentary for early signs of the 2027+ project-credit cliff, and any direct management comment on the securities suit.

30-day (early August): Section 232 ruling — the still-pending binary; favorable/CdTe-neutral outcome reinforces BUY toward the $300-320 stretch case, an outcome that extends tariff relief to SE-Asian polysilicon-based competitors cuts the differentiation case toward the bear range.

60-90 day: Securities class-action developments (lead plaintiff appointment after 8/24/26 deadline, any motion to dismiss); 45X-extension-draft legislative progress (post-midterms, a 2027+ item, not a near-term thesis break); TOPCon ITC 337-TA-1494 outcome.

Flips to AVOID: an adverse/neutral-to-competitors Section 232 ruling, a Q2 guidance cut where underutilization charges exceed the 45X credit floor, any legislative move against the current 45X manufacturing credit itself, or a securities-suit development revealing materially new negative facts beyond the known Feb 2026 guidance cut.

Flips to higher conviction: a favorable Section 232 ruling landing near current levels (confirms the sell-side upgrades were right and still leaves entry room), a clean Q2 print with backlog commentary confirming the 2027+ demand runway, or a reversal to insider buying.

Research dossier: SNDK — Sandisk Corporation

Business

Pure-play NAND flash maker (spun out of Western Digital), co-producing 3D NAND with Kioxia

through a JV running to 2034, now in 10th-generation 3D NAND production — capex-light bit

scaling standalone competitors can't replicate. Customers are hyperscalers, enterprise-storage

OEMs, and the channel, paying for capacity and price-per-bit. The current revenue surge is the

AI-memory supercycle: datacenter NAND demand outrunning a supply base that has added almost no

new wafer capacity, anchored partly by Sandisk's "New Business Model" (NBM) — multi-year,

fixed-price, take-or-pay contracts (~$42B backlog, ~$11B enforceable customer guarantees)

covering roughly a third of FY27 bits. The durability debate is unchanged and still the whole

question: NBM anchors ~1/3 of bits; the other ~2/3 reprice at spot when the shortage normalizes.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Yes, small and fractional — today (2026-07-13) delivered exactly the liquidity event the last

two dossiers said to wait for, and it arrived harder and cleaner than the 7/6 version.

What happened since the 7/6 dossier ($1,744.43, BUY 0.55/52): SNDK continued grinding down

through the week to ~$1,915 by mid-July (still up huge YTD, "+700%" per Gurufocus), then **today

SK Hynix's ADR debut coincided with a Korea Investment & Securities note cutting SK Hynix's

operating-profit estimate ~8% below consensus — specifically because HBM/DRAM pricing is rising

slower than expected** — and the entire memory cohort cratered: SK Hynix −15% (worst single-day

move on record per Motley Fool), Samsung down hard, Micron/SNDK/the Roundhill Memory ETF all

20% off recent highs ("bear market" per Yahoo Finance). SNDK itself fell −12.6% today alone

to $1,673.97 (stockanalysis.com, fetched, matches the screen's $1,673.32 close).

Three things make this a cleaner entry than 7/6's:

SK Hynix's miss is about HBM pricing lagging estimates — a DRAM product SNDK doesn't even

product's earnings estimate cut. Per macro-cohort-confirmation, this is about as

textbook "liquidity, not information" as a drawdown gets — the informational content for

SNDK's own product is close to zero.

but still a rising-price quarter, not a flat/declining one. The 7/6 dossier's "first crack"

claim doesn't hold up under a direct source check; treat that framing as retired.

Research dossier: UBER — Uber Technologies, Inc.

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 55

Next earnings: 2026-08-05

Business

A two-sided demand-aggregation marketplace across Mobility (ride-hail), Delivery (Eats/grocery),

and Freight. Uber takes a cut of gross bookings routed through the network; riders/eaters and

drivers/couriers are the two sides, and Uber One (~50M members, >50% of bookings) is the retention

flywheel. Durability rests on the marketplace moat: two-sided liquidity (199M MAPCs, +17% YoY as of

Q1) compounds with scale, and in theory monetizes whoever supplies the ride — including

third-party AV fleets riding on Uber's demand graph. The franchise is structurally FCF-generative

($2.3B FCF in Q1 alone), not a cash-burner.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Still a buy, but the entry edge is thinner and the central bear risk (AV disintermediation) got a

concrete, negative data point since the last run. Q1 2026 (May 6, still the latest print — Q2

reports Aug 5) was an acceleration quarter: bookings $53.7B (+25% YoY, +21% cc), revenue $13.2B

(+14%), trips 3.64B (+20%), non-GAAP EPS $0.72 (+44%), $3B buyback, Uber One 50M. No new

fundamental print has landed in the two weeks since my prior 06-27 run — the stock is trading

sideways-to-down on sentiment, not new numbers. What did change: on **June 29, Waymo and Uber

ended their robotaxi pilot in Phoenix** — a small deployment (~a dozen vehicles), with Waymo

redirecting those cars to DoorDash delivery and Via transit rather than expanding the Uber

integration. Riders can still reach Waymo directly via the Waymo app. Commentary (The Driverless

Digest) frames this as the "first concrete chip" in Waymo pulling back from the Uber-partnership

model, and flags Austin/Atlanta — Uber's two much larger, exclusive Waymo integrations (hundreds of

vehicles each) — as the names to watch next. Nothing has actually moved in Austin/Atlanta yet, and

Waymo's own July 8 expansion (San Diego, Las Vegas, Tampa, Denver, initially employees-only) is

independent capacity growth, not evidence those markets are going Uber-exclusive or Waymo-direct.

Net: the AV-disintermediation bear case, which was a slow-burn 2028-2030 debate in my prior dive,

now has one small, real, negative data point on the Uber side of the ledger — not a break, but

exactly the kind of thread the falsification section said to watch, and it fired before the next

earnings print.

Micron is one of three global DRAM/NAND makers (with SK Hynix and Samsung), together ~89% of

global DRAM supply. DRAM (server/data-center + increasingly HBM) is the bulk of revenue; NAND

the remainder. Historically the most cyclical semiconductor vertical — oligopoly pricing swings

the P&L violently. The 2025-26 structural change is HBM as a discrete, high-ASP sub-market

driven by GPU training/inference: Micron is #3 in HBM share (~21-24% vs SK Hynix ~43-62%,

Samsung ~17%) but is NVIDIA's swing supplier for HBM4 dual-sourcing, now in volume shipment of

HBM4 for Vera Rubin. Customers have locked ~$22B in take-or-pay long-term supply contracts —

paid regardless of actual offtake, a real change to the demand-visibility picture vs. prior

cycles. Micron is also announcing up to $3B in incremental U.S. investment (concrete poured at

a new NY fab) and holds a GM automotive supply deal plus the 2026-06-22 Anthropic multi-year

HBM/DRAM/SSD supply + co-design agreement (with a direct stake in Anthropic's Series H).

Research dossier: CIEN — Ciena Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.5 · Opportunity score: 52

Next earnings: 2026-09-03

Business

Ciena designs and sells optical networking hardware, software, and services. The flagship is

WaveLogic coherent optics (the DSP-driven modems that push data down long-haul and data-center

fiber — 800G shipping, 1.6T qualifying), plus packet/routing platforms and a network-management

software layer. The newest product is RLS Hyper-Rail, an intelligent line system co-created

for AI-training interconnect across hundreds of kilometers.

Who pays them: historically Tier-1 carriers (AT&T, Verizon, BT), but growth has fully rotated to

hyperscalers building data-center interconnect (DCI) — the fiber links between AI data

centers carrying petabits/second, plus the DCOM out-of-band management product scaling at Meta

and a second hyperscaler. Ciena is the incumbent leader with proprietary DSP silicon and 20+

years of deployment density. Revenue durability rests on: (a) 7–10-year optical equipment

lifecycles; (b) the operational catastrophe of switching optical vendors mid-build; (c) a

hyperscaler capex wave (~$725B for 2026, +77% YoY) still mid-cycle. This is a substrate bet —

picks-and-shovels paid every time a hyperscaler lights another DCI link

(orchestration-vs-substrate).

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Closer to yes than the 2026-06-30 read, and for a specific reason: the price has fallen back to

roughly where my own discipline said to buy, and the proximate cause of the fall looks more like

indiscriminate sector beta than a Ciena-specific fundamental problem.

What changed since June 30 ($490.56 → today $460.74, a real ~6% net move but with much larger

intraday swings — screen shows a 52-week high just 27.7% above today's price, meaning CIEN

touched $637 very recently before round-tripping down through the $418–440 range and partially

recovering):

1. June 9 — SemiAnalysis co-packaged-optics (CPO) "delay" report triggered a ~7% CIEN slide

alongside Lumentum (-8%). This report is about switch-side CPO adoption timing — a

technology aimed at intra-rack/switch interconnect, not Ciena's core long-haul/DCI pluggable

business. Ciena is also a participant in the Open CPX MSA (announced March 2026), i.e.

positioned on both sides of the pluggable-vs-CPO debate, not a pure pluggables incumbent

with existential CPO exposure. Read as: the market traded CIEN as a "photonics" beta name on

a headline that bears less directly on its actual product mix than the tape implied. This is

an inference, not a confirmed sourced fact — flagging it as the load-bearing uncertain claim

in this dossier (see Falsification).

2. July 2 — cohort-wide "high-beta AI-infrastructure" reset. CIEN -8.65% same day as

Applied Optoelectronics (-17%), Coherent and Lumentum (-10% each) — explicitly reported as a

valuation-driven sector rotation, not Ciena news. No Ciena-specific 8-K or guidance change

accompanies it.

3. June 11 — $2.875B 0.00% convertible notes due 2031 closed (upsized from $2.0B), initial

conversion price ~$746.66, effective conversion price raised to ~$1,000/share via bond-hedge

+ warrant overlay. Proceeds repaid ~$1.14B of the term loan and repurchased ~0.3M shares.

Net effect: ~$1.7B of net new zero-coupon debt, dilution economically hedged unless the stock

more than doubles from here — a manageable balance-sheet move, not a red flag, but it does

raise gross leverage and is worth tracking into the Sept print.

4. No fundamental update: Q2 print (June 4), $7.7B backlog, FY2026 $6.3B guide, the single

Hyper-Rail multi-rail award (Meta) are all unchanged. No second Hyper-Rail award confirmed.

Net read: this is not "extended without catalyst" (June 30's problem) or "extended with

catalyst" (no new positive fact either) — it's **compressed by cohort beta on a report whose

direct relevance to Ciena's actual business is contestable**, with the balance sheet move being

a second, smaller drag. That is a different, more actionable setup than a melt-up on no news.

optionality on a second revenue line that didn't exist two weeks ago.

Research dossier: MDB — MongoDB, Inc.

Researched: 2026-06-30 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.57 · Opportunity score: 50

Business

MongoDB sells a document-oriented database platform. Two revenue buckets:

  • Atlas (cloud-managed, consumption-based) — the growth engine, ~75% of total revenue,

grew 29.4% YoY in Q1 FY2027 and added a record $117M of dollar net-new ARR in one quarter

(four straight quarters of >29% growth). Multi-cloud, serverless, with vector search,

text/time-series search, and stream processing folded in natively — the bet is collapsing a

separate vector store + operational DB + feature store into one managed surface, and becoming

the persistent-state layer for AI agents going to production. (orchestration-vs-substrate:

MDB is an orchestration-side data layer, not GPU substrate — its AI exposure is workload

demand, not the capex J-curve.)

  • Enterprise Advanced + Other (self-managed license + support) — mature, ~+13% YoY,

high-margin, declining share of mix.

Who pays: dev-centric enterprises building modern apps — fintech, e-commerce, gaming, real-time

personalization, AI-agent backends. The document model's schema flexibility fits when data shape

evolves fast (i.e. every AI product in production). Atlas is sticky once pipelines are built on

it. Durability: high.

Last print — Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-04-30): revenue $687.6M (+25% YoY), an

acceleration from the ~22% trough; non-GAAP op margin 18% (up from 16%); non-GAAP EPS

$1.32 (vs $1.18 est.); a small GAAP net income of +$4.4M (TTM GAAP still −$29M). TTM

revenue $2.60B (+23.6%). No new print since — the next data point is the Aug 27 Q2 report,

so fundamentals are unchanged from the May 28 print.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Support held. Catalyst didn't change. So the verdict shouldn't either — it's a hold-of-support

Research dossier: NRG — NRG Energy, Inc.

Researched: 2026-07-10 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 50

Next earnings: 2026-08-04

Business

NRG is an integrated independent power producer (IPP) + the largest competitive retail

electricity supplier in the US, weighted to Texas/ERCOT and PJM, with a ~25.8 GW generation

fleet after the Jan 30, 2026 close of the ~$12B LS Power acquisition (+13 GW gas/dual-fuel +

the CPower virtual-power-plant platform). Revenue is (1) selling power/retail plans to ~8M+

homes/businesses (sticky, the higher-quality book) and (2) merchant wholesale generation — a

price-taker spread on ERCOT/PJM clearing prices. The growth leg is selling firm power to AI

data centers via the GE Vernova + Kiewit/TIC development agreement (up to ~5.4 GW new gas gen,

1.2 GW by 2029, 1.2 GW by 2030, ~3 GW 2030–32) plus ~445 MW of signed retail data-center

contracts (a 295 MW Texas deal + 150 MW PJM add). This is the AI Energy Thesis expressed

through a large, cash-generative incumbent, but on the grid-connected merchant side —

behind-the-meter gas (Williams–Meta, VoltaGrid, BE) routes around NRG. NRG captures AI load

second-hand, via tighter clearing prices and capacity auction results, not a direct

contracted on-site moat.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Yes, modestly — at $140 the margin of safety has partly returned, and the crux variable the

last two dossiers flagged is now moving the right way.** Since the 2026-06-27 dossier (HOLD @

$149.36, "at fair value, wait for a pullback or a signed confirm"), NRG did exactly what the

entry-shape base rate implied it might: it pulled back to $136.70 (Jul 2) before stabilizing

around $140.34-$140.42 (Jul 10) — a real ~6% retracement from the June high, not the full

$134 re-engage level from the prior dossier but a genuine step back toward it. More

importantly, the fundamental crux variable — ERCOT/PJM forward power prices — has produced its

first real forward-looking confirming data since the Q1 miss: ERCOT North Hub is projected up

~45% in 2026 vs 2025 with summer on-peak forwards at $110-165/MWh and ERCOT forecasting

a new all-time peak demand record (90,500-98,000 MW vs the 85,508 MW 2023 record), driven

explicitly by data-center load. Separately, PJM's 2027/2028 capacity auction (cleared Dec 2025)

hit the FERC price cap at $333.44/MW-day, a fresh record (+1.3% over the already-record

2026/27 auction), with PJM now falling short of its reliability target for the first time —

~5,100 MW of the shortfall directly attributed to data-center load growth. This is the

connectivity, and security silicon — tier-1 auto suppliers and OEMs (~56% of revenue), plus

Business

Subscription streaming at global scale — ~325M paid memberships (the company no longer

recurring and sticky; the durable engine now has three legs: (1) core subscription pricing

power, (2) the paid-sharing/extra-member crackdown that converted freeloaders into payers, and

(3) a fast-ramping ad tier guided to ~$3B in 2026 (a doubling YoY). TTM revenue $46.89B

cash-generative, high-margin compounder — not a capex J-curve name and not AI-infra.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

At $72.88 the stock is down ~42% off its highs and sitting ~1.5% above its 52-week low — a

real dip, not an extended chase. The fall is a cluster of name-specific sentiment shocks,

not a fundamental break: (1) Netflix lost the Roku bidding war to Fox — its second failed

high-profile M&A pursuit, raising capital-allocation questions; (2) co-founder/board chair Reed

Hastings declined re-election at the June 4 AGM, which LightShed's Greenfield said is "spooking

investors"; (3) Q2 guidance came in light ($12.57B rev vs $12.63B consensus; $0.78 EPS vs

$0.84); (4) Meta expanding Instagram-for-TV to Samsung sets in the US adds a competitive

overhang. None of these breaks the earnings engine — revenue still +16.7%, margins still

catalysts are recent and unresolved (leadership, M&A discipline, competition), the print is 24

days out and just guided down, and the dip-buy base rate for this name is poor.

Research dossier: FORM — FormFactor, Inc.

Researched: 2026-07-14 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 46

Next earnings: 2026-07-29

Business

FormFactor makes probe cards — the precision electro-mechanical interfaces that contact

wafers during semiconductor test to verify die before packaging. It is the dominant half of a

premium duopoly (with Italy's Technoprobe): probe cards are co-developed with each customer's

process node, switching costs are high, and the R&D cadence to keep pace with new packaging

generations is a real barrier.

The demand driver is HBM — the stacked DRAM in every AI accelerator. Each HBM generation

(HBM3E → HBM4) needs materially higher probe-card complexity, lifting ASPs and volumes together.

Customers: SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron, TSMC, leading OSAT/foundry partners. The Dec 2025 **Keystone

Photonics** acquisition adds optical wafer-test for silicon photonics/CPO — a 2026–2028 TAM

extension, already in the narrative, not a fresh catalyst.

Nothing about the business changed since the last dive (2026-06-17). What changed is the price.

hard: $126 (Jun 5) → $140 (Jun 17, my last HOLD-at-stretch call) → ~$116 today, a -27.4%

pullback from the $160.27 52-week high and roughly back to the early-June level. Two things distinguish

~12× forward earnings / ~10% FCF yield, near its 52-week low, after a ~33–38% YTD drawdown.

Q1 FY27 (reported 2026-05-27) was a clean beat — revenue $11.1B (+13% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $3.88

(+50%), FY27 guide raised to $45.9–46.2B, and a $25B accelerated buyback that puts a real

floor under the share count. Agentforce ARR hit $1.2B (+205% YoY), and 7 of the 10 largest Q1

deals added seats — directly contradicting the disruption narrative. The market is pricing

terminal-value impairment into a business still growing double digits and gushing cash.

The catch: the de-rate is a thesis-narrative dip ("SaaSpocalypse"), not a liquidity dip.

Per macro-cohort-confirmation, cohort-wide weakness driven by information (will AI agents

collapse seat-based SaaS?) changes the thesis rather than simply creating a clean entry.

Organic growth has decelerated to ~9% (Tableau/marketing/commerce soft), Agentforce is still

<3% of revenue, and the resolving catalyst — proof of H2 reacceleration or Agentforce reaching

material scale — has not landed. So: cheap and well-defended, but the overhang is real and

unresolved. Not a high-conviction at-market buy here.

historical 25–40× and bakes in skepticism. The 12× today implies the market doubts the seat

model survives agentic AI, not merely that growth has slowed. Analyst avg target $255 (+54%) is

the un-discounted bull read; I weight it as an anchor, not a base case.

Not applicable in the Wait-for-deal thesis sense — there's no lab-partnership deal to

whether the structural bear case is right, not whether the move is already in the price.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

plus into a hawkish-dot scenario.

low rate sensitivity — that lifts it above the extended-AI-infra median. But the unresolved

disruption overhang plus the weak dip base rate keep it short of a standout. Net: a constructive

HOLD / watch, score 45 — interesting enough to track for the trigger, not the marginal $100 today.

A week of real, positive fundamental news, and the stock is exactly where it was. Since the

(7/7, 8-K): revenue growth accelerating to ~29% YoY (from 22% in Q1, 14% in the year-ago

despite genuinely better underlying numbers. That's the headline tension this dive has to

resolve: is this a buyable dislocation (market ignoring real acceleration) or a correctly-priced

Research dossier: ESTC — Elastic N.V.

Researched: 2026-06-08 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 42

Business

Elastic is an enterprise search, observability, and security platform company built on the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana). Three pillars: (1) Search — hybrid keyword + vector search, now marketed as "The Search AI Company" powering enterprise RAG applications; (2) Observability — log analytics, APM, infrastructure monitoring; (3) Security — SIEM/XDR. Revenue is >90% subscription, ~80% sales-led. Customers are deeply embedded: the ELK stack is load-bearing infrastructure for search and logging across thousands of enterprises; migration costs are high.

FY2026 full-year revenue: $1.739B (+17% YoY). $100k+ ACV customers: 1,660+. $1M+ ACV customers: >240. Net Expansion Rate: ~112%. AI use cases now penetrate >1/3 of the $100k ACV cohort; AI-using cohorts expand ~5% faster than baseline. AI backlog: >$1B as of Q4 FY26 (May 2026 report).

Why revenue continues: The installed base is structurally sticky (search indices, log pipelines, SIEM rules are not moved lightly). The enterprise-sales motion is converting larger multi-year deals — record $1M+ deal quarter in Q4 FY26, and customers with $5M+ ACV growing ~30% YoY. The platform bet (one vendor for search + observability + security) creates consolidation tailwinds vs. running three point solutions.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

As of June 8, 2026 — 12 days after Q4 FY26 earnings — the answer is: compelling valuation, awkward timing; wait for a cleaner entry.

The business case is genuine:

  • FY27 revenue guidance: $1.985–$2.0B (~15% YoY). Non-GAAP operating margin guided to ~19% (targeting 25% by FY29). FCF margin ~21.5% in FY27 → ~$430M free cash flow on a $6.35B market cap = ~6.8% FCF yield. For a 15% grower with margin expansion, this is dramatically cheap vs. software peers.
  • EV/forward sales: ~2.7x (peer group: Datadog ~10x, CrowdStrike ~18x, MongoDB ~10x). Even applying a steep discount for Elastic's competitive pressures, 3x the current multiple is defensible.
  • AI search positioning is real. Hybrid search (keyword + vector) is the dominant enterprise pattern for RAG applications — Elastic has been doing hybrid search longer than the pure vector DB startups. The $1B+ AI backlog gives near-term revenue visibility.

The timing tension: the Q4 FY26 beat (revenue $451M vs. ~$440M estimate, profitability turn, FY27 guidance) already landed on May 27 and the stock popped +24% from ~$50 to ~$62. That catalyst has been absorbed. The principles mandate: "demand a real dip OR a fresh catalyst." At $62 post-bounce, neither condition is cleanly met. A macro-induced pullback to $52-58 would restore the asymmetry needed to justify a new buy.

Conclusion: fine business, real value, not the right moment to add at $62. HOLD; watch for the re-entry.

52-week range: $42.05 – $96.07

How much is already priced in: the FY26 beat and FY27 guidance raise are in the price. The AI backlog converting to consumption revenue acceleration — if it materializes in FY27 earnings prints — is not fully in the price yet.

ESTC is not a Wait-for-deal thesis name. It's an established public company with no pending hyperscaler partnership the market is waiting on.   • Bear: AWS OpenSearch permanently impaired the open-source moat, Datadog owns observability mindshare, CrowdStrike/Splunk own enterprise SIEM, and 15% growth at decelerating trend is the ceiling, not the floor — re-rating never comes.
  • First-principles: A business generating $430M in annual FCF from $2B in enterprise revenue, growing at 15% with sticky installed base and hybrid-search AI positioning, should trade at more than $6.35B; at the current price you are buying real cash flows cheaply, not speculating on a thesis.

Research dossier: GEV — GE Vernova

Researched: 2026-06-09 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.60 · Opportunity score: 42

Business

GE Vernova (spun from GE, April 2024) is the energy-technology company with three segments:

1. Power (~$23B revenue) — gas turbines, aeroderivatives, nuclear steam, gas engines. The sold-out core. Gas turbine slot reservations have grown from 83 → 100 GW through Q1 2026, targeting 110 GW by year-end. New equipment pricing running 10–20% above Q4 2025 levels in a seller's market.

2. Electrification (~$13.9B projected 2026, +44% YoY) — grid transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems, software. Data-center-driven demand is the growth engine: $2.4B in data-center equipment orders in Q1 2026 alone, more than all of 2025 combined. Book-to-bill ~2.5x.

3. Wind (~$7B) — offshore and onshore wind; still margin-challenged but improving. Not the thesis driver; margin drag remains.

Who pays them: utilities, hyperscalers, independent power producers, grid operators globally. Power and Electrification revenue is long-cycle (backlog → execution over 3–5 years). Services contracts on installed base provide a durable recurring stream once gas turbines are shipped.

Why it continues: hyperscaler AI buildout is inelastic to GEV's pricing; the grid-upgrade backlog for HVDC and transformers is multi-year regardless of macro. GEV's only scaled competition in gas turbines is Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi — no new entrant can build that manufacturing capacity in years.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The AI energy thesis is as directly applicable here as anywhere in the field. Power IS the binding constraint, and GEV is the picks-and-shovels supplier. Q1 2026 results confirmed the thesis is accelerating, not decelerating:

  • Orders +71% organic to $18.3B — not a one-quarter fluke; driven by both gas turbine reservations and electrification
  • Backlog at record $163B (+$13B sequential), now targeting $200B by 2027 (one year ahead of prior plan)
  • Gas turbine slots filling through 2030: pricing power is locked in for years, not quarters
  • Guidance raised to $44.5–45.5B revenue / 12–14% adj. EBITDA / $6.5–7.5B FCF for 2026

The question isn't whether GEV is a great business — it demonstrably is. The question is whether $939 is a good entry. The stock has already run from ~$458 a year ago to a high of $1,182, then pulled back 21% to $939. In an extended market with 3.8% CPI and no rate cuts until fall 2026 at earliest, the current pullback reflects macro multiple compression rather than fundamental deterioration. That's encouraging for the business but doesn't resolve the valuation question: at ~37x 2026 FCF, you are paying for the continued strong execution of an already-proven story.

Verdict: HOLD. The business is excellent, the pullback from peak is real (21%), but the price is at/near fair value for THIS macro environment. I'm not finding a genuine margin of safety at $939.

Valuation + position vs. range

Using FCF multiple for a high-quality industrial with pricing power and backlog visibility:

  • 30x 2026 FCF ($7B) = $210B market cap → $778/share (deep-value entry, demanding a discount)
  • 35x 2026 FCF = $245B → $907/share (fair; captures pricing power + backlog premium)
  • 40x 2026 FCF = $280B → $1,037/share (stretch; requires rate cuts to justify)
  • 45x 2026 FCF = $315B → $1,167/share (analyst consensus range; priced for perfection)

At $939, the stock trades at ~37x 2026 FCF — between my fair (~$907) and stretch (~$1,037) bands. Not cheap; not obviously broken.

Using 2027 FCF (if growth trajectory continues to ~$9–10B), the picture looks better: 25–28x — more defensible for a business of this quality. But that requires continued execution through an uncertain macro.

GEV is post-IPO (April 2024) and post-multiple-re-rate. The stock was in the $100s at spin; the AI-energy thesis became widely appreciated through 2025 and the stock ran accordingly. At $939, this is not a "pre-deal" entry. The 21% pullback from the $1,182 peak is meaningful, but the 52-week run of +105% makes clear the entry-edge from the pre-recognition phase has been consumed.

The extended-with-vs-without-catalyst check: the Q1 2026 blowout (April 22) is a FRESH thesis-confirming catalyst — orders +71%, backlog record, guidance raised. Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bear: At 37x 2026 FCF in a rising-rate, no-cut environment, the multiple has nowhere to go but down until the Fed actually moves, and the Wind segment is still a margin anchor.

Current price ~$939 is sitting just below the "fair" band entry, slightly above buy-below. The pullback from $1,182 has created a marginally more interesting setup than a month ago, but I don't want to pay "fair" in this macro — I want to pay "buy-below."

Macro fit

Kill-switch status: All three clear. Capex growth far from threshold; GPU pricing/lead-times in generation-transition only; credit spreads historically tight. The secular AI buildout is intact — no structural kill on the demand side for GEV's products.

Regime: Extended. S&P trailing P/E 25.3x, CAPE 42.3x, Buffett Indicator 237%. CPI at 3.8% with no cuts expected until fall 2026 at earliest. This is a multiple-compression environment for premium-multiple industrials, not a multiple-expansion one. GEV at 37x FCF in this regime requires the business to re-rate through earnings growth rather than multiple expansion — that's possible (2027 FCF of $9-10B would cut the multiple to 25-28x at current price), but it takes time.

Opportunity-cost rank: Compared to the field:

  • vs. cash (3.5–3.75% risk-free): GEV's FCF yield is ~2.7% on 2026 guide — actually below cash yield. You're betting on continued FCF growth, not yield.
  • vs. other AI-energy names (BTM gas, nuclear, electrification): GEV is the highest-quality but also most-priced. Smaller/earlier-stage power names may offer better risk/reward on the same thesis.
  • In the opportunity-cost cross-section: GEV is a "hold and wait for $880" rather than "buy now at $939." The May CPI print (June 11, two days away) is a near-term catalyst for the macro; a cool print could re-rate the stock toward $1,000+, a hot print could push it toward $880.

Score: 42/100. Excellent business, but at ~fair value in a compressed-multiple macro. Not the marginal best use of fresh capital today.

Falsification

60-day: Q2 2026 orders/guidance (July earnings) — the $18.3B Q1 order print set a high bar. If Q2 orders slow (say below $12–13B), the backlog narrative cracks. If they hold above $15B, the $200B backlog-by-2027 target looks credible. Watch for Electrification data center order continuation (Q1 was $2.4B vs. all of 2025 — is this a one-time pull-forward or a new run-rate?).

90-day: Wind segment margin trajectory — if Wind gross margins turn positive on a sustained basis (vs. currently sub-zero on some programs), GEV's consolidated margin guide has upside. Flip: if offshore project charges recur, the margin guide comes in at the low end.

Thesis-flip to BUY: Price drops to $850–880 (30–32x 2026 FCF) with fundamentals intact. OR: Q2 2026 orders come in above $16B and guidance is raised again — that would be a fresh catalyst justifying a buy even at $939.

Thesis-flip to AVOID: Multiple hyperscaler capex guidance reductions (kill-switch #1), a sustained pullback in Electrification data-center orders, or Wind charges large enough to impair the FCF guide materially below $6B.

Research dossier: TER — Teradyne, Inc.

Researched: 2026-07-14 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.5 · Opportunity score: 42

Business

Teradyne sells automated test equipment (ATE) — the machines chipmakers, foundries and OSATs

use to verify silicon works before it ships — plus an Industrial Automation arm (Universal

Robots cobots, MiR autonomous mobile robots). Semi Test is the engine (~87% of Q1 FY26 revenue,

~70% of that AI-related per Q1 commentary). Revenue durably continues because every AI

accelerator, HBM stack and advanced-package die must be tested, and test intensity rises with

chiplet/HBM complexity. Management's own framing (CEO Gregory Smith, cited via TIKR): the ATE

market grows from ~$9B (2025) to $12-14B, with Teradyne's share moving from ~30% to ~35-38% —

memory/HBM growth is explicitly the swing factor. No new business-model facts this run; this is

the same franchise as the 07-04 dive, now trading on a third leg down.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Ten days after the last dive ($369.09), the stock has kept falling: **$353.16 today, now 27.6%

off the 52-week high (vs. 24.4% off on 7/04), intraweek low $334.35 on 7/13**. Two distinct

sell-offs have now stacked on top of each other, and they are NOT the same shape:

1. 7/2 (already priced into the 07-04 dive): cohort-wide capex-sustainability fear (Citi

questioning hyperscaler spend), Philly Semi -7%+, no TER-specific news.

2. 7/13 (new since last dive): SK Hynix's biggest one-day drop on record (-15%, South

Korea), triggered by a Q2 profit estimate ~8% below consensus that multiple snippet sources

attribute to slower-than-expected HBM4 shipments. This one lands closer to TER's own bull

pillar than 7/2 did — HBM/memory test demand is the specific growth driver management is

counting on for the ATE TAM expansion above. Micron also fell (-4.3% on 7/13) sympathetically.

This is the genuinely new, load-bearing fact this run, and the read on it is contested. A

snippet-level search result frames it as HBM4 shipment-timing weakness (bearish for the memory-

test thesis specifically); a separate fetched analysis (investing.com) argues the broader July

move is actually about hyperscaler capex-efficiency worry (MSFT CFO disclosed ~$25B of its

~$190B capex is component-inflation, not new capacity) and circular-financing anxiety, NOT a

memory-demand breakdown — with memory shortage still "forecast to last through 2028" and Micron

signing 16 new customer agreements. I could not settle which read is right from today's sources;

it is exactly the ambiguity the July 28 print needs to resolve (see note below).

Two things argue this is still closer to noise than thesis-break: (a) all three

ai-infra-thesis-kill-switches remain untripped (capex guidance unchanged ~$725B/+77% YoY,

Research dossier: CRDO — Credo Technology Group Holding

Researched: 2026-07-13 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 41

Next earnings: 2026-09-09

Business

Credo sells the physical-layer plumbing that moves bits inside AI data centers. Its anchor

product is the AEC (Active Electrical Cable) — copper cables with Credo SerDes silicon baked

into the connector — which has displaced pluggable optics for short in-rack/rack-to-rack hops on

cost and reliability. Since the DustPhotonics acquisition (closed May 2026) it also owns

silicon-photonics PIC capability, targeting an in-house 800G-3.2T optical stack (>$500-600M FY27

optical revenue guided), and has separately been building **Hyperlume-derived Active LED Cables

(ALCs)** as a second, MicroLED-based hedge against CPO — Credo is running two parallel bets to

diversify away from pure-AEC exposure rather than standing still. Who pays: hyperscalers building

AI clusters. Customer concentration remains the defining structural fact — top two customers

~84-87% of revenue in recent quarters (carried figure, still unverified against the primary

10-Q/10-K — flagged again this run). That's who pays, and also why the revenue is fragile to any

single customer's architecture decision.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Since the 2026-07-04 dive (HOLD, $241.85, opportunity 36), the stock has **drifted lower to

$236.70 (screen, Jul 13 close) — a further ~2% decline, and now 23.2% off the June 22 ATH**

of $308.67 (vs. 21.6% nine days ago). The key change this run is what's driving the weakness,

not new company-specific news:

1. No new CRDO-specific developments. No fresh CPO design-out evidence, no customer news, no

revised guidance. The Nvidia/Coherent $2B optics investment that keeps surfacing in searches

is March 2026 news, already stale and already priced through the June dives — not a new

catalyst. Continued routine insider selling (CTO Chi Fung Cheng, ~3,790 shares July 8, part of

the same 10b5-1 pattern as the ~$76.9M combined CEO/CFO/CTO/CLO/director selling flagged in

the prior dive) — profile unchanged: profit-taking under pre-scheduled plans, all filers retain

large stakes, not a fresh signal.

2. Today's -8.1% single-day move is a clean, verified cohort event. SK Hynix suffered its

largest single-day drop on record (>15%) in Seoul trading on July 13, triggering a broad

global semiconductor/AI-hardware selloff that hit Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Micron,

Western Digital, Seagate, and Sandisk alongside CRDO — explicitly described as post-IPO

profit-taking after SK Hynix's Nasdaq debut, not an AI-demand or CRDO-specific repricing.

Per macro-cohort-confirmation, this is materially cleaner than the July 4 read,

Research dossier: SITM — SiTime Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-04 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.62 · Opportunity score: 41

Business

SiTime makes MEMS-based precision timing semiconductors — oscillators and (post-Renesas) clock

ICs that are the heartbeat of virtually all electronics. MEMS timing is a structural upgrade

over quartz: smaller, lower power, superior jitter, no piezoelectric aging. SiTime is the

dominant pure-play with ~60% of the MEMS timing market. Revenue is led by Communications,

Enterprise & Datacenter (CED), up ~158% YoY in Q1 2026; AI/datacenter is the primary engine —

as inference clusters densify (PCIe 5/6, 800G/1.6T Ethernet, high-radix switching), timing

tightness rises, so higher GPU density = more MEMS content per rack.

What's new since the 2026-06-27 dive: the Renesas timing-business acquisition **closed on

2026-07-01** — materially earlier than the "year-end 2026" close previously guided. SiTime now

owns the ~$300M-revenue, ~70%-gross-margin, ~75%-AI-Datacenter-Comms clock business outright: a

new $200M senior secured revolving credit facility (Wells Fargo, closed June 30) sits alongside

the $1.2B 0% convert (May) and the $900M term loan as the funding stack; Renesas received ~4.13M

SiTime shares (now outstanding, with registration rights) plus a board seat for CEO Shibata.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The underlying business quality is undisputed and, if anything, strengthened: the deal that was

an open integration risk two weeks ago is now closed six months ahead of schedule, converting a

"pending, financed" story into a "done, operating" one. That is a real de-risking event, not

just a data point — the two biggest tail risks in the 06-27 dossier (deal falls through / slips

into 2027; the debt stack sits unused for months) are both resolved in the bull's favor.

The market's reaction was the opposite of a re-rate up: -14.6% (to $601.66) on 07-02, then

another leg down, bringing the stock to $601.57 by today (screen), a -15.7% 20-day return

and now sitting -12.5% below its 50DMA (was -0.4% on 06-27) and +39.6% over the 200DMA

(down from +58.8%). Searches found no fresh negative business fact behind the drop — no guidance

cut, no lost design win. The likeliest read (consistent with the 06-27 QuiverQuant framing that

called this an ongoing "financing overhang" story, now crystallizing at close): the market is

pricing the immediate, concrete dilution — 4.13M shares now actually outstanding rather than

a future contingency, registration rights for Renesas to sell into the market, and a fully drawn

leverage stack ($1.2B convert + $900M term loan + new $200M revolver) — against a business that

was already trading at ~47x trailing sales. Closing early removes integration-timeline risk but

crystallizes the dilution/leverage the market had been discounting only partially.

Per extended-with-vs-without-catalyst: is this a fresh catalyst or a re-confirmation? The

deal closing on-thesis, just early, is confirmation of the standing bull case, not a new one —

but the price reaction is real and moves the entry math. This is now the **best entry point

since the deal was announced in February** — genuinely closer to the $560-660 fair band this

desk derived two weeks ago, not just a shallow pullback from an already-rich price.

Lam Research is one of the three dominant wafer-fabrication-equipment (WFE) makers, alongside

Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron. Its franchise is etch and deposition — the tools that

carve and layer 3D structures in leading-edge logic and especially 3D NAND, where Lam is

share leader. Customers are the chipmakers (TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, Intel). This sits

service/spares ("CSBG") tail on the installed base. Revenue durably continues because every

node transition and new fab is more etch/dep-intensive, and the installed base throws off

high-margin service regardless of the equipment cycle. Nothing about this business logic has

changed since the last dive.

a routine executive-liquidity pattern, not a fresh signal (the FSLR dive on 2026-07-07 found the

Research dossier: TSM — Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.

Researched: 2026-06-19 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.6 · Opportunity score: 40

Next earnings: 2026-07-16

Business

The world's dominant pure-play foundry — it manufactures the leading-edge logic (and increasingly the advanced packaging) that everyone else designs. Customers are the fabless ecosystem: NVIDIA, Apple, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm. Revenue durably continues because TSM is a near-monopoly at the leading edge (3nm/2nm) and the binding bottleneck of the AI buildout. This is the "wafers" half of Gavin Baker's "watts and wafers" — and per Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability and GPU Economics, TSM's restraint (disciplined capacity adds run by "flinty old-school veterans") is what smooths and elongates the cycle by preventing an overbuild. Wafer intensity may be AI's savior; TSM is the toll booth.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The business is firing on all cylinders, but the entry is the question, and at ~$462 (0.6% off the 52-week high, +34.6% over 60d, +37.9% above the 200DMA) this is an extended chart. Q1 2026 (reported Apr 16): revenue $35.9B (+6.4% QoQ USD), gross margin 66.2% (record, beat the high guide by 120bp), operating margin 58.1%, HPC 61% of revenue (+20% QoQ). They raised full-year 2026 revenue-growth guidance to above 30% in USD and guided Q2 to $39.0–40.2B (+10% QoQ) at 65.5–67.5% GM. Research dossier: BTDR — Bitdeer Technologies Group

Researched: 2026-06-20 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.5 · Opportunity score: 38

Business

Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ: BTDR) is a Bitcoin miner executing a funded pivot into AI/HPC data-center infrastructure. Founded by Jihan Wu (Bitmain co-founder). Three revenue legs: (1) self-mining BTC — still the dominant engine (70.2 EH/s self-mining hashrate, 83.1 EH/s under management as of May 2026); (2) mining hosting / cloud hashrate; (3) AI Cloud — early GPU colocation + cloud (ARR ~$69M at 90% utilization, 4,248 GPUs deployed). It designs its own ASICs (SEALMINER line; A4 at 9.45 J/T, plus the DL1 Hydro Scrypt rig) for internal use and sale — the in-house silicon is a genuine cost edge over miners buying third-party rigs.

The durable differentiator is power-advantaged sites inside a stated ~3GW global power portfolio: Norway (Tydal — Phase 1 50MW + Phase 2 175MW, hydro, Nvidia Vera Rubin reference design, both phases now targeted for Q4-2026 energization) and a 570MW Clarington, Ohio site (power under contract with AEP). Management has explicitly reframed the story: colocation, not BTC appreciation, is the compounding bet, and "executing colocation lease agreements" is named top priority.

Why AI-colocation revenue would durably continue: cheap Norwegian hydro + EU data-sovereignty pull create real demand for EU-based AI compute. The open question is unchanged across three dives now — the anchor customer is still unsigned, so pricing power and customer quality remain unconfirmed.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Still pre-customer, and the net of the last 7 days is mixed-to-slightly-negative. The Tydal tenant is "in advanced negotiations" — but that exact phrase appeared in both the May and June updates, so the headline fact hasn't actually advanced. Meanwhile Clarington just picked up a fresh negative (litigation delay). Neither the "fresh-catalyst" nor the "real-dip" gate is open.**

This is a textbook Wait-for-deal thesis structure: power-rich, Nvidia-aligned sites ahead of a signed hyperscaler/AI-lab anchor. If a named customer signs the Tydal lease this reprices hard (the BE-post-Oracle "sustained repricing" pattern is the analog). Applying extended-with-vs-without-catalyst's operational test — what fact about the business changed in the last 7–14 days? — the honest answer:

  • Tydal: still "advanced negotiations," no signature. The language is now a month stale; protracted negotiation without close is a mild yellow flag, not a catalyst.
  • Clarington (NEW, negative): the 570MW Ohio site is delayed by legal proceedings filed by a neighboring company (American Heavy Plate Solutions LLC); no energization timeline given. This narrows the near-term colocation surface to Tydal alone.
  • Production: 921 BTC mined in May (+370% YoY), record hashrate — strong operational color, but mining is the gross-margin-negative leg, so volume isn't the value driver.

So the run (+35% 20d, +118% 60d, +30% vs 200DMA) is momentum without a thesis-confirming fact — the FOMO frame is the correct one. Don't chase.

Fundamentals remain uncomfortable: Q1 gross margin was -20.7% (deteriorated from -5.7% a year ago), Q1 net loss $159.5M, TTM net income -$199M.
